package_info.package_versions: v1.16.1 and prior (core and plugins as described)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains multiple critical vulnerabilities (Reflected XSS, Stored XSS, SQL Injection, Session Fixation) that allow attackers to execute arbitrary code in users' browsers, extract sensitive data from the database, and hijack user sessions. These vulnerabilities stem from improper input sanitization, insecure session management, and unsafe file handling.

required_permissions: user interaction (victim must visit crafted URL)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, user-supplied GET/REQUEST parameters 'sort' and 'order' are concatenated into variable names and HTML attributes without proper sanitization, allowing injection of arbitrary HTML/JS into the DOM, resulting in Reflected XSS.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Direct use of user input in HTML attributes without robust sanitization enables XSS.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would sanitize or encode user input before inserting into HTML; here, input is used directly.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic table sorting, but should use whitelisted values.
key_indicators: User input directly concatenated into HTML attributes

required_permissions: user interaction (victim must visit crafted URL)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, user-supplied 'type' and 'state' parameters are inserted into an anchor tag without sanitization, allowing Reflected XSS via crafted input.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Untrusted user input is embedded in HTML output without encoding.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected to sanitize or encode all user-supplied data before output.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic export links, but should use whitelisted/encoded values.
key_indicators: User input directly in HTML output

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, user-supplied 'order' parameter is concatenated directly into an SQL ORDER BY clause without validation, enabling SQL Injection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: User input is used directly in SQL query construction.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected to validate or parameterize all user input in SQL queries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic sorting, but should use a whitelist of allowed columns/directions.
key_indicators: User input in SQL ORDER BY clause

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At login, the application does not invalidate the existing session or issue a new session cookie, allowing an attacker to set a session ID before authentication and hijack the session after victim login (Session Fixation).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Session ID is not regenerated on authentication, enabling fixation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected to always issue a new session ID on successful login.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; session fixation is always a vulnerability.
key_indicators: Session cookie not changed after login
Ability to set arbitrary session ID

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<?xml version="1.0" standalone="no"?>
<!DOCTYPE svg PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD SVG 1.1//EN" "http://www.w3.org/Graphics/SVG/1.1/DTD/svg11.dtd">
<svg version="1.1" baseProfile="full" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
   <rect width="200" height="200" style="fill:rgb(0,255,255);stroke-width:3;stroke:rgb(0,0,0)" />
   <script type="text/javascript">
      alert("Stored XSS!!");
   </script>
</svg>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user uploads a file containing SVG with embedded JavaScript, the file is served without sanitization, resulting in Stored XSS when accessed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: SVG files with embedded scripts are not sanitized or served with safe headers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected to sanitize SVG or serve with Content-Type/image headers to prevent script execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate SVG uploads, but must sanitize or restrict scripts.
key_indicators: SVG files served with embedded JavaScript

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious URL or file upload exploiting XSS or SQLi.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim visits URL or accesses file, triggering XSS or SQLi.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript executes in victim's browser (XSS) or attacker extracts data via SQLi.
attack_chain.leads_to: Session hijack, privilege escalation, or data exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages session fixation to hijack authenticated sessions.

behavioral_signatures: User input reflected in HTML output without encoding
User input used directly in SQL queries (ORDER BY, etc.)
Session cookie not regenerated on login
SVG files with embedded scripts served as-is
network_indicators: Unusual GET/POST requests with suspicious parameters (e.g., order, type, state) containing script or SQL payloads
Session cookies reused across login boundaries
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for user-supplied parameters being reflected in HTML responses without encoding, especially in admin or export pages. Scan for SQL queries constructed with unsanitized user input. Check for session cookies that are not regenerated on login. Inspect uploaded SVG/XML files for embedded scripts and ensure they are not served with executable content types. Use SAST/DAST tools to identify these patterns and monitor logs for suspicious access to file_uploads directories.
